note: Baseline 20 PPI questions from content_data.py converted to bank format. All users get these 20 questions with age/experience filtering.

items.prompt: When making financial decisions, I prefer to:
options: A Research extensively before deciding
B Go with my gut feeling
C Ask friends or family for advice
D Follow what experts recommend

items.prompt: My approach to saving money is:
options: A Save a fixed amount each month
B Save whatever is left over
C Save only for specific goals
D I struggle to save consistently

items.prompt: When I think about my financial future, I feel:
options: A Excited and optimistic
B Anxious or worried
C Uncertain but hopeful
D Confident and prepared

items.prompt: I track my spending:
options: A Daily or weekly
B Monthly
C Rarely or never
D Only when I'm worried about money

items.prompt: My biggest financial priority right now is:
options: A Building an emergency fund
B Paying off debt
C Saving for a specific goal
D Learning to budget better

items.prompt: When I receive unexpected money, I usually:
options: A Save most or all of it
B Spend it on something I've wanted
C Split it between saving and spending
D Use it to pay bills or debt

items.prompt: I learn best through:
options: A Reading and research
B Hands-on practice
C Watching videos or tutorials
D Discussion and conversation

items.prompt: My relationship with credit cards is:
options: A I use them responsibly and pay in full
B I avoid them completely
C I sometimes carry a balance
D I struggle with credit card debt

items.prompt: When setting financial goals, I prefer:
options: A Detailed plans with specific timelines
B General direction without strict deadlines
C Short-term goals I can achieve quickly
D Long-term vision with flexibility

items.prompt: Financial stress affects me by:
options: A Making me more motivated to improve
B Causing me to avoid thinking about money
C Impacting my sleep or mood significantly
D I don't experience much financial stress

items.prompt: I would describe my spending habits as:
options: A Very disciplined
B Mostly controlled with occasional splurges
C Impulsive at times
D Often reactive to emotions

items.prompt: My knowledge of investing is:
options: A Strong – I actively invest
B Basic – I understand the concepts
C Limited – I'm just starting to learn
D None – It seems too complicated

items.prompt: When facing a financial setback, I:
options: A Quickly adjust my plan and move forward
B Feel discouraged but eventually recover
C Need support from others to cope
D Find it very difficult to bounce back

items.prompt: I prefer to make purchases:
options: A After careful comparison shopping
B When I find a good deal
C When I need or want something
D Impulsively if it feels right

items.prompt: My comfort level with financial risk is:
options: A High – I'm willing to take calculated risks
B Moderate – Some risk is okay
C Low – I prefer safety and stability
D Very low – I avoid risk completely

items.prompt: I talk about money with friends/family:
options: A Openly and regularly
B Occasionally when relevant
C Rarely – it feels uncomfortable
D Never – it's too personal

items.prompt: My biggest financial challenge is:
options: A Not earning enough
B Controlling my spending
C Understanding financial concepts
D Staying motivated to save

items.prompt: When planning my budget, I:
options: A Use detailed spreadsheets or apps
B Keep a rough mental estimate
C Follow a simple system
D Don't really budget

items.prompt: I would describe my financial personality as:
options: A Planner and saver
B Balanced and practical
C Spontaneous spender
D Still figuring it out

items.prompt: My motivation for improving financial literacy is:
options: A Achieving specific financial goals
B Reducing stress and anxiety
C Building long-term wealth
D Feeling more confident and in control
